title: Rework
author: Jason Fried and David Heinemeier Hansson
blurb: Rework is a short, punchy manifesto from the founders of 37signals, the company behind Basecamp. They argue that much of the conventional wisdom about starting and running a business is outdated or simply wrong. You don't need outside investors, a detailed business plan, a big team, or eighty-hour weeks. Instead, they urge readers to start small, build something they personally need, and treat limits on time, money and people as advantages. They champion cutting features until only the essential core remains, launching before things feel perfect, and saying no far more often than yes. They also take aim at workplace habits that quietly destroy productivity, especially meetings and constant interruptions. The result is a practical, contrarian guide to doing better work with less stress, less waste and far less ceremony.

lessons.b: The warnings people give about how business 'really works' are mostly excuses, and you can build something on your own saner terms.
Long-term business plans pretend to predict an unknowable future, so it's smarter to decide what to do next based on what you know now.
The best products come from solving a problem you have yourself, and ideas mean little until you actually start making something.
